articles.content:
Noomi Rapace is venturing into the film and TV production space by officially launching Boom Films, co-founded with her longtime manager and production partner Stella Härnström. The London and Stockholm-based company is being backed by former Pulse Films boss Thomas Benski ’s Lumina Media .

The actor, who first captured global attention with her potent portrayal of Lisbeth Salander in the Swedish film adaptations of Stieg Larsson's Millennium Trilogy — starting with “The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo" — is ramping up a slate that currently comprises six to eight female-driven genre projects. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'You Can See Everything' Gets Digital Release ‘One Last Order’: Beloved Drive-Thru Worker Sighle Williams Says ‘I Miss the Community’ as Viral Netflix Doc Streams

"I've done a lot of action movies, and I've always been craving to work more with women," she told Variety. "But in so many of these films, it's me fighting men. So it's the same thing with male directors in the action [movies] sphere. Where are all the women that want that direct action?"

Boom is joining Lumina Media’s growing portfolio of businesses comprising Carrousel Studios, founded by Omar Sy, Louis Leterrier and Benski; Benedict Cumberbatch’s SunnyMarch; Yann Demange’s Wayward Films; Magna Studios, which is behind Oasis doc "Don't Look Back in Anger" and headed up by fellow former Pulse execs Marisa Clifford and Davud Karbassioun; gaming and creator economy business Creators Corp; and Arcade Media.

Lumina Media will work closely with Boom Films as a strategic partner. Besides making an unspecified investment, Lumina will provide "development expertise, commercial support and access to its international network, helping the company progress its existing slate and scale the business," according to a statement. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Oskar Pimlott, who is a former head of film at Vice and Pulse Studios, has been appointed head of film at Boom Films. Pimlott is working alongside Rapace and Härnström to develop Boom's slate, which is being kept under wraps for now, with the first projects to be announced early next year. Pimlott was recently nominated as a breakthrough producer at the British Independent Film Awards for his work on Swedish director Jonatan Etzler’s black comedy “Bad Apples.”

Boom will be working directly with filmmakers and artists to develop original projects from the ground up. "Its slate spans action, thrillers, horror and supernatural stories aimed at global audiences, alongside prestige arthouse cinema developed in collaboration with world-leading filmmakers," according to the statement. The company also aims to create original stories and IP with the potential to extend beyond film and television into other formats.

"Boom Films sort of came out of this desire to connect dots; to connect people," Rapace, who has previously served as producer on several projects, most of which she starred in, told Variety.

"I've worked with all these incredible filmmakers and actors and producers and writers all over the world," she added. "But it takes so long from an idea to sending out a film to the world. And a lot of momentum gets killed because it's too many middle hands."

Added Benski: "From the Lumina perspective as an investor, what was very attractive is that Noomi and her team are a real engine. They are really builders and I've been so impressed with what they've been able to build so far, very much in stealth. The reason for the investment is to help amplify them."

Benski noted that Lumina intends to be "a bridge between Scandinavia, Europe and the U.S." and that, in terms of financing, they "might take a big swing" on some of the projects, while others will "need market validation" from outside investors as well.

Benski said the plan is for Boom Films to start rolling out projects strategically next year "during the next few markets and festivals."

As for the company's name, Rapace said that Boom "stands for the heartbeat, but also explosions," adding: "I've always loved films that sort of explode into your mind and heart, and you don't need to always love them, but you need to remember them and sort of go back to them." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Describing the slate, Rapace said it will comprise very well known IP "approached from an innovative angle," underlining that it will be about "embracing this difference to create specificity," and the budgets will be "quite varied."

Rapace said she will be starring in several of the projects in the Boom Films slate. Like many other actors who venture into production, she is now mulling plans to debut as a director — in her case, with a comedy.

"I have a really dark sense of humor, and I'm really drawn to comedies. Even though everyone sees me as this very serious, hardcore [actor], like, 'Oh she's so badass!'" she said. "But my son is always telling me, 'You're such a nerd.' So I think maybe I'd like to direct a stupid comedy — something I've never done. Maybe that's where I need to go."

articles.title: 'Hershey' Review: In a Sugary Sweet Biopic, Finn Wittrock Plays the Candy Man Who Turned Chocolate Into an American Empire
articles.summary: At "Hershey," you feel like you’re 10 years old again, which is both a virtue and not. The film is a paint-by-numbers storybook biopic for the chocolate-loving child in us all – or, maybe, for an audience the movie treats as if it needed its hand held.
articles.content:
Angel Studios, in its quest to deliver movies that remind us of The Way America Used To Be, has brought back the "great man" biography — not so much the old-fashioned Hollywood biopic but, rather, movies like "Young Washington" and " Hershey ," the sort of life-of-the-plaster-saint saga you used to read in the fifth grade. These are history-based tales that are proud in their simplicity, that abolish all shades of gray, that are intended to inspire but also work on the audience because they’re so comforting . It feels good, in a certain super-square regressive way, to watch a movie about the man who popularized the American chocolate bar and was a paragon of philanthropic generosity besides. At "Hershey," you feel like you’re 10 years old again, which is both a virtue and not. The film is a paint-by-numbers storybook biopic for the chocolate-loving child in us all — or, maybe, for an audience the movie treats as if it needed its hand held. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'The Odyssey' Oscar Campaign Kicks Off With 8 New Revelations, From Tom Holland’s Shorter Skirt to Pattinson’s Rejected Wig and a Trojan Horse Stuck in Customs 'The Odyssey' Takes Imax to Biggest Quarterly Revenue to Date

Early on, there’s a scene that gives you that kid-in-a-candy-store feeling, because it’s all about…a kid in a candy store. Milton Hershey, played as a boy by James Kelly, has moved with his stern 19th-century Mennonite family from a dairy farm in Pennsylvania Dutch country to the bustling city of Lancaster. There, he wanders into a candy shop, where he’s welcomed by the owner and chief candy maker, played with a touch of screwball carny fervor by Richard Kind. "There’s no sweeter way to make a living," he says, offering the boy a candy called a sugar-plum swirl and then taking him under his wing as an apprentice. Milton learns the art of candy, and it’s not long before the film cuts to Philadelphia in 1882, where the adult Milton now has his own candy store with a handsome green-and-white awning. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

He makes hard candy and yummy taffy, but his specialty is caramel bonbons, which he crafts with a special milk recipe. It’s the milk that gives it that luscious velvet smoothness. Milton has got the goods, and he’s a charismatic candy man besides. Finn Wittock, a veteran of Ryan Murphy series (and also "La La Land" and Mike Nichols’s 2012 stage revival of "Death of a Salesman"), is a likable actor who suggests a cross between Orson Welles and Robert Wagner. He’s got a sonorous elegance and gleaming eyes, but with a user-friendly nice-guy veneer. For Milton, making candy is a mission, but he starts off as a faltering businessman; his shop goes under, and that will happen to him again, as he struggles to find an audience for his goodies. Salvation comes in the form of a British aristocrat (Mark Ashworth) who tastes one of Milton’s caramels and puts in an order for 3,000 of them to be shipped to England for a party.

"Hershey" is a movie in which the hero has obstacles (like his unscrupulous candy-business rival), but no demons or inner conflicts. He’s just like his candies: sweet on the outside and the inside. For a while, caramel is king, but it’s chocolate that’s the future. The film colors in the period when Milton is leveraged up to his eyeballs and still searching for the perfect recipe; he figures out that milk is the key here as well. But the aspect of Milton Hershey the movie is actually most interested in is that he popularized what had formerly been elite candy. The Swiss and British chocolates that inspire him are all based on secret recipes, and they’re so expensive that few can afford them. Hershey wants to make a great candy bar that will sell for five cents, so that anybody can buy one. He pays his workers top dollar and gives them shares in the company. He’s a turn-of-the-century Willy Wonka as utopian socialist dreamer.

Wittrock makes Hershey appealingly robust in his chocolate passion, and that drew me into the movie. What keeps nudging me out of it was how sketchy it is. "Hershey" was directed Mark Waters, who did lively work in the late '90s and 2000s ("Mean Girls," "The House of Yes"), but here he skitters through a script that’s so perfunctory it treats even the invention of the Hershey’s Kiss as just one more oh-and-this-happened incident. The dew-drop-shaped candy first results from a faulty machine, but we never see Milton — or anyone else — rhapsodize about it, sharing with the audience what makes it so special. (They never even mention the silver-foil wrapping.) My own theory of the Hershey’s Kiss is that it’s a magical candy because it’s made of the very same chocolate as a Hershey bar, yet that succulent shape somehow makes it taste different. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Milton meets and marries the feisty Kitty (Alexandra Daddario), who loves him, spars affectionately with him, and inspires him to establish a school for impoverished children. But the desire to move back to his old homestead and build an entire town in Pennsylvania Dutch country — the factory town of Hershey, which will be part workers’ paradise, part Disneyland — is his own. They’re living the dream until Kitty starts to succumb to muscle seizures, and it turns out she has a degenerative illness, progressive paraplegia. The movie refuses to characterize her condition as tragic, but it does use it to inspire what we might call faith-based tears.

"Hershey" is a movie that makes you hungry for chocolate, and that’s part of its appeal. So is the notion that a legendary American entrepreneur could ever have been this much of a selfless gentleman. Yet the movie simulates your sweet tooth without necessarily satisfying it. Chocolate, as anyone who craves it knows, is no casual delight. There’s something orgasmic about chocolate (yes, even a Hershey bar), but in "Hershey" it’s a strictly civilized pleasure.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There are some movie vehicles that need no introduction and the Batmobile is one of them. As one of the most iconic movie cars ever seen on screen, the idea of owning the real thing is one that would likely be just the stuff of dreams. However, someone is now the proud owner of Michael Keaton's Batman Returns Batmobile, one of three built especially for Tim Burton's 1992 sequel and based on the designs of the original 1989 Batmobile. The version auctioned by Julien's Auctions was the action hero car, a true one-off piece of movie history that has now been purchased for an astonishing $4.39 million , although even that huge amount is something of a disappointment considering it came in under the original estimates of between $5-7 million.

The Batmobile that has now sold was the first vehicle delivered to the set for the production of Batman Returns and the auction house notes that there are several pieces of evidence that prove this is the vehicle that appears on screen in the majority of the movie's driving sequences, and it was driven by Keaton in many of those scenes. As you would expect, there are many reasons why the 1989 Batmobile would probably have sold for more than a copy made for its sequel, but a $4.39 million price tag is certainly not small change and is one of the most expensive movie props ever sold at auction. The sale was part of a larger auction, which also included many other Batman items such as Keaton's cowl/chest piece, Alicia Silverstone's Batgirl costume piece from Batman and Robin, and several pieces from the more recent Batman vs Superman and Justice League movies.

When it comes to iconic movie vehicles, a 2004 poll by UCI Cinemas put Keaton's Batmobile at the top of the list of the best screen cars ever, ahead of James Bond's Aston Martin and the minis from The Italian Job. While some people still prefer other Batman cars, with Adam West's 60s version getting an honorable mention on some polls and Christian Bale's Tumbler leading the pack in others, on the whole, there is a general consensus that the 1989 version and 1992's copycat are the ultimate iterations of one of the coolest vehicles in cinema. That is why it has been recreated in toy lines, LEGO sets, artwork and many other mediums over the years, more than any other Batmobile seen across the numerous Batman projects that have been released in the last 60 years.

However, there is nothing like the real thing, which is why this auction attracted so much attention since it was originally announced last month. In 1992, there were many Batman fans who would have never imagined that one day the actual Batmobile they were watching on screen would be sold to the highest bidder. Perhaps if they had, they might have invested money wisely over the last three decades to have a shot of putting in a bid that could snatch victory at hammer-fall. It is hard to imagine that this Batmobile will appear on the auction block again anytime in the near future, but whenever it does show up somewhere down the line, there is a strong chance it could end up selling for more than it did in this event. Maybe it is time to start saving up now for when that eventually happens.

How much would you pay to own the Batmobile? Let us know in the comments.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The passing of Patrick Stewart on Oct. 28, 2026 was a huge shock to the entertainment industry and the millions of fans who loved his prolific body of work across the different series he performed in. Unbeknownst to the majority of the world, Stewart's cause of death was revealed as a “brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the latter of which was the same devastating affliction Robin Williams was secretly dealing with before he took his life. Whatever struggles Stewart dealt with during his final days may forever be a secret, but what we do know is that fans will have one more chance to see him in action when Professor X joins the battle against Doctor Doom in Avengers: Doomsday later this year.

According to an interview with Entertainment Weekly , Feige and the Russos are planning on having a tribute to Stewart in Doomsday , but how that looks has not been entirely decided at this time. “We’re long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us,” Feige told EW. “We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.” Feige also revealed that Stewart was offered a role in the upcoming Secret Wars film, but turned it down. Whether this was health-related or he passed for other reasons will likely never be known.

Regardless of his reasons, Doomsday will be Stewart's final appearance as the headmaster of the Xavier Institute as previously reported on this site . As the incursions on the Multiverse by Doctor Doom wreak havoc on many worlds, many believe this entry in the franchise will be a bittersweet one for the mutant side of the MCU, and may very well be the end of this on-screen iteration of Professor X. The future of the character is uncertain, but one sad note that is true is that Doomsday was the final role Stewart would perform.

Feige recalled that last day on set, and how heavy it felt after it happened. "He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew. We didn’t know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.” Anthony Russo added to the sentiment, calling it a "very emotional" moment. “I think it was in the back of all of our heads, we may never see him on set again… It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence." Russo believed the effects of whatever Stewart was going through were hidden by the veteran actor as much as possible, but they sensed something was different about him and appreciated the full effort Stewart delivered. "For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.”

Rumors about what Marvel Studios will do to honor Stewart's memory have ranged from an "In Memorium" at the conclusion of the film, to a custom opening logo sequence focused on his performances through the years as Professor Xavier. It's a challenge to figure out one way to honor the man when he has given so much to different fandoms over the years. To many, he is their Star Trek captain, and to others he is there Professor X — let alone not forgetting the many other impactful roles Stewart played on stage and screen. One moment will never feel like enough to honor the legend who crossed fandoms and elevated whatever genre he took part in, giving 110% to each role he undertook.

After the news of Stewart's passing broke, tributes from his colleagues poured in . Feige commented on the announcement not long after, writing “It was a true privilege to know him and to work with him. His legacy lives on not only in decades of extraordinary work, but in the many, many people he mentored. He will be deeply missed.” Hugh Jackman wrote "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days.”

How do you hope that Doomsday will honor the memory of Patrick Stewart, and how are you feeling a month after this sad news broke? Let us know in the comments and check in with your fellow grieving fans.

articles.title: 5 Weird ’80s Movies That Every Gen X Kid Watched, And That Explain Why We’re All Messed Up
articles.summary: If there is one thing that you could say about Gen X it’s that they really don’t make ‘em like they used to. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If there is one thing that you could say about Gen X it’s that they really don’t make ‘em like they used to. Particularly when it comes to the later group of Gen Xers, this is a group of people who are independent and self-reliant having largely grown up having to fend for themselves, remember life before the digital revolution made everything weird, and are honestly a little dark and twisted in terms of humor. Very little phases a Gen Xer — and a bit reason for that are some of the weird movies we watched when maybe we shouldn’t have.

Here are five movies — some released in theaters, some aired on television because someone thought that was a good idea — that are absolutely wild that just about every Gen X kid probably saw in the 1980s and, if we really think about it, explain an awful lot about why we are the way we are now. We’re also throwing in an honorable mention that truly gives insight into just how cynical we are — and it has an absolutely stacked cast.

Let’s start off with that honorable mention because it might be the most “normal” movie on this list. Released in 1986, River’s Edge is a crime drama that has a wildly great cast, especially in retrospect. It starred Crispin Glover, Dennis Hopper, Daniel Roebuck, Keanu Reeves, and Ione Sky in her film debut (though she’s credited as Ione Sky Leitch in this film). The movie follows a group of teenagers but don’t get it twisted that this will be some sort of high school story like a John Huges film gone serious. This is the darker side of the American teen experience and these teens are completely emotionally disconnected, so much so that when one of the group murders his girlfriend, the rest have pretty much zero reaction, at least at first.

The film is a slow burn of things subtly working their way out of control, with a tight narrative that reveals how numb and directionless the teens are without the adults in their lives paying attention. Darker and darker things get revealed. Gen X is largely considered to be cynical and detached as a personality trait these days and River’s Edge is a brilliant snapshot of exactly how that played out in a way that was more “real” than the pop culture of the time would let you believe. Also, it’s abundantly clear how great of a talent Reeves is here.

Now that I’ve thoroughly bummed you out with River’s Edge , let’s get into the weird stuff. In 1985, CBS offered up a two-part, made-for-television special that on the surface sounds innocent enough: a musical adaptation of Lewis Carrol’s Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland and Through the Looking-Glass . It was broadcast just in time for the holiday season that year across December 9th and December 10th. It was absolutely stacked with its cast — we’re talking Sammy Davis Jr., Telly Savalas, Ringo Starr, Carol Channing, and even John Stamos. It was very book accurate, with the first night taking on the first book and the second taking on book two.

The special was also creepy as all get out. The entire production was live action, which meant that the fantasy characters required elaborate costumes on a 1980s scale. the hookah smoking Caterpillar (played by Davis Jr.) is a wild, just off Technicolor cousin of the Dune sandworm. Starr’s Mock Turtle looks like a cat. But the real nightmare fuel here was the weirdly wet-looking Jabberwocky . Imagine a giant sticky larvae with wings, T-rex arms, glowing eyes and horns, wandering around menacing people while, and I cannot stress this enough which is why I say it again, looking sticky and moist. And we haven’t even touched on the parts of the story where humans are turned into live animals. You might be able to still find this one on some corners of the internet if you dare but, seriously, beware the Jabberwock.

Another television moment, in 1983, the Disney Channel aired a special, Hansel and Gretel . The live-action short came from the now-legendary Tim Burton and was surprisingly faithful to the original Brother’s Grimm story, but how it made its way to the faithful nature of that story left small 80s kids pretty much scarred for life. Burton took the German fairy tale, gave it an entirely East Asian cast , incorporated a kung fu fight between Hansel and Gretel and the evil witch who uses candy canes to fight with (that part is actually very cool). It didn’t shy away from any of the darkness of the actual story, either.

But what makes this absolutely weird is just how disturbing various elements are. The special has a character, Dan Dan the Gingerbread Man, who sings a twisted cover of Rod Stewart’s “Da Ya Think I’m Sexy?” while trying to coerce Hansel into eating him piece by piece. Dan Dan is also a very demented looking, colorful puppet. There is also the fact that Vincent Price is the host. It’s twisted nightmare fueled served up as children’s entertainment and that should tell you everything you need to know about Gen X.

Now, every Gen X kid watched The Wizard of Oz on repeat thanks to it being broadcast on television pretty regularly and usually around the holidays, but it’s the 1985 Disney follow-up, Return to Oz that falls right into that sweet spot of “this is a weird movie that we all saw and probably messed us all up.” The film starred Fairuza Balk in her feature debut and gave us a faithful adaptation of L. Frank Baum’s work — more so than the OG classic movie. It picks up after Dorothy comes back from Oz and things aren’t great for her but they aren’t great in Oz either and she soon goes back to deal with a new threat there.

Return to Oz is a dark and disturbing film that borders on body horror. We start with Dorothy about to get electroshock therapy because everyone thinks she’s crazy. Once we’re in Oz, the movie’s primary villain is one who has a glass cabinet full of severed heads that she changes out like most people change outfits and she has big plans to make Dorothy’s head one of them. Then there’s the Wheelers rather than flying monkeys and they’re scarier than all get out. Even the audio is sort of messed up. Dark, twisted and twisted in a kind of familiar and oddly pretty way, that’s how you sum up Return to Oz and it’s definitely something that left a mark on Gen X.

1982’s The Dark Crystal is without question an absolute masterpiece and probably one of the most important fantasy movies of all time. From Jim Henson and Frank Oz, it was the first of kind as a major live-action movie that had no human actors and relied instead on elaborate, groundbreaking animatronics. The world was elaborate, complex, and stunning in its tale of the planet of Thra and specifically of Jen and Kira, two Gelflings on a quest to restore balance to their world and overthrow the evil rule of the Skeksis. It is a really good movie, especially in retrospect.

But try being a kid in the 1980s watching it. The Skeksis? They’re huge, disgusting buzzard-like monsters that are more than a little homicidal. Jen and Kira are small, delicate things and there’s a sequence where you see Gelflings having their essence drained from them that is absolutely horrific. Sure, these are puppets and animatronics, but you can’t unsee the violence and horror — especially when some part of you is seeing these characters as strange versions of like, Big Bird.

You can’t have a Gen X movie list without Heathers. Coming in right at the end of the 80s in 1989, Heather’s might be the funniest movie on this list and maybe the least horrifying. Consider this Gen X’s Mean Girls, just darker. Starring Winona Ryder and Christian Slater, it took the John Hughes high school world of it all and took it dark, making the quest for popularity and peer pressure actually lethal. Like, literally, someone dies by drinking a mug of drain cleaner.

If River’s Edge spoke to the alienation and disconnect of Gen X, Heather’s did the same but flipped into something a bit more palatable and added the painful parts we didn’t want to talk about: the way being alienated from mainstream teen culture as it was fed to us could feel as well as what our distrust for authority actually looked like. It is also a very quotable, quippy film and while Heather’s definitely shaped us, of all the movies on the list, this one probably best explains us. It also still holds up after all this time, kind of like Gen X itself.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday did a clever job of giving us some deeper insights into what the emotional core of the story will be. Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) will be presented with the dilemma of how his actions with the Infinity Stones at the end of Avengers: Endgame caused major cracks in the Marvel Multiverse that have led to the Doomsday event of mass incursions. It will be especially tough since Steve is now fighting for his beloved family (his son and Peggy Carter) and not just his world.

However, while the Final Trailer for Avengers: Doomsday may be doing a lot to position Steve Rogers as the main character the film hinges on, there are a lot of theories that it's all a major misdirect. Marvel Studios and directors Joe and Anthony Russo may have an entirely different kind of storyline for Doomsday – one that goes back to a familiar well of success.

What we know about the MCU version of Doom so far (besides being played by Robert Downey Jr.) is that he, too, is seeking means to preserve life and existence as the multiverse collapses, but that he's willing to achieve that goal in more nefarious ways than our heroes. The film after Doomsday, Avengers: Secret Wars , is based on a 2015 comic book crossover event, where incursions wiped out the Marvel Multiverse, except for a single reality called "Battleworld," which Doom manifested by stitching together pieces of the doomed realities. Battleworld was broken up into 41 territories (or "domains"), each governed by a "Baron" or "Baroness." The Barons included characters like "Emperor" Shang-Chi, Spider-Man (ruler of "Spider-Island"), Apocalypse, the avatar of Konshu, a "Witch Queen," and Hulk's malevolent variant, "Maestro," to name a few.

While no one should expect to see a 1-to-1 adaptation of the Secret Wars comic story, I still believe that Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars are borrowing heavily from that crossover event. In short: Doom will need a collection of superpowered individuals to create his new reality in the film – or, more specifically, he'll need their power . And when it comes to the goal of avoiding the end of existence and starting a new one, only omega-level powers will do.

If you don't know the term: in Marvel Comics lore, "omega" is the ultimate level of power ranking for mutant heroes and villains. It is distinguished as power with no known upper limit, and characters like Magneto, Jean Grey, Professor Xavier, and Storm are all prime examples of it. For the MCU and Avengers: Doomsday , however, "omega" is just a reference point for the level of power Doom is after. Powers he will either steal himself or utilize by entrancing the characters he needs, in order to create and maintain his new world.

Either way, the clues are already out there that this is indeed how Avengers: Doomsday is approaching things: Doom making a heist just like Thanos in Avengers: Infinity War, and stacking powers like Infinity Stones. Just look at the list of targets that are either on the board already (Hulk, Scarlet Witch , Franklin Richards), or are already confirmed to show up and battle at some point in the film. Each one of them either has the power to create and build a new world, influence/control the people in it, or decimate any challengers who would try to stop or undo it.

That's just a rudimentary list of who Doom could siphon and/or kill to gain top-tier power. We didn't even count a mystical character like Doctor Strange, who may not have a superpower to steal, but could still be used as Doom's personal servant ("Boris") alongside the "Latverian Witches," 3 mystery characters whose mystical power will also be harnessed in service of Doom. That potentially sets up some big character cameos, if Strange, Scarlet Witch, and two other prominent mystics (Sylvie? Clea?) are revealed to be the ones behind the Witch masks.

There could also be some surprise characters who pop up as targets: Jean Grey has been conspicuously absent from the X-Men lineup, but would be a pivotal surprise cameo if the original actress, Famke Janssen, returns. Her powers (and the Phoenix Force she's previously hosted) would make Doom unstoppable. Monica Rambeau and her powers as Photon are also worth consideration, and some fans have long held the belief that a variant of Josh Brolin's Thanos will also be on Doom's capture list.

Do you think Doom is really on the hunt for the biggest powers across the superhero multiverse? Let us know your take (and some possible big cameos who would be targets) in the comments! Avengers: Doomsday will be releaed on December 18th.

Jenna Ushkowitz doesn't want to remember when  Glee  did a tribute to Cory Monteith after his death.

Philip Rosenberg , the production designer who won an Oscar for his work on All That Jazz and also worked on films such as Network , Moonstruck and The Hurricane , has died , according to his nephew, Alan Rosenberg. No cause of death was given. He was 91.

Rosenberg was raised in Brooklyn before studying scenic design at Yale University with Donald Oenslager. About that time, he was hired as an assistant at the Metropolitan Opera where he worked with Ita Maximovna and Eugene Berman. His first film was The Seagull in 1968, on which he was a design assistant.

Among Rosenberg's first starry projects was Herbert Ross' The Owl and the Pussycat in 1970. Rosenberg was the art director on the film starring Barbra Streisand and George Segal. articles.title: Doomsday Just Shattered a Disney Record But One Avenger Still Has The Movie Beat
articles.summary: Less than one month before its release, Avengers: Doomsday just shattered a major Disney record, suggesting that the film is on the path to box office success; however, there is still one Avenger whose movie is the one to beat, and even Doomsday may not pull it off. Doomsday hits theaters on Dec. 18, and […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Less than one month before its release, Avengers: Doomsday just shattered a major Disney record, suggesting that the film is on the path to box office success; however, there is still one Avenger whose movie is the one to beat, and even Doomsday may not pull it off. Doomsday hits theaters on Dec. 18, and it seems like Marvel is doing everything in its power to make sure all eyes are on the movie. Earlier this week, the final trailer of the movie was released, which stirred up plenty of fanfare and had viewers realizing some big things, from the fact that Thor is getting a massive upgrade to a tease of the Young Avengers potentially joining the MCU .

In addition to that trailer and its many reveals, new interviews have confirmed some significant Doomsday details—including a clearer explanation of the separation between Iron Man/Tony Stark and Doctor Doom from Robert Downey Jr. himself and a clarification about why certain X-Men won't be in Doomsday —and a newly released teaser offered a first look at Steve Rogers and Thor facing off against Doctor Doom . Now, on top of all of that, it's been confirmed that the brand-new trailer broke a massive Disney record (but it still hasn't beat one other MCU movie).

According to Deadline , Doomsday has already broken a major Disney record, with the new trailer getting 563 million views in its first 24 hours. This makes it the single most-viewed Disney trailer of all time, which is obviously a very impressive feat and suggests that the movie may be well on its way to a box office success. However, it still hasn't topped the record-shattering Spider-Man: Brand New Day . Per the same article, this Doomsday trailer is the second most-viewed movie trailer of all time, behind none other than Brand New Day . That trailer, by comparison, got 718.6 million views in its first 24 hours.

Although this is just a conversation about the trailers, it does open up other questions about the comparisons to come between Brand New Day and Doomsday . For one, many are wondering whether Doomsday will be able to beat out Brand New Day in terms of the many, many records it broke this summer. Doomsday does have a fair shot at some of these titles, though, including the highest-grossing movie of all time at the domestic box office. After all, franchises like the MCU and Star Wars consistently top these lists, with Avengers: Endgame still holding the worldwide box office record and Brand New Day have beaten out Star Wars: The Force Awakens domestically.

Given that Doomsday is not only an Avengers movie but also a highly-anticipated one that fans have been waiting seven years for, there's plenty of reason to believe it could ultimately smash these records. However, if the trailer is any indication, it still might not be enough to beat out Brand New Day .

articles.content:
Six Indonesian projects, each from a director-producer pairing working on a debut or sophomore feature, have been chosen for the 2026 Indonesia-France Film Lab X MTN Lab, which runs Nov. 25-30 in Yogyakarta as part of JAFF Market .

Now in its third edition, the lab is run by the French Embassy and the Institut français d'Indonésie (IFI), with French film school La Fémis supplying the mentors. Indonesian partners include the Ministry of Culture's Directorate of Film, Music and Arts, through its national talent management program, MTN, as well as the Indonesia Film Agency (BPI) and the Association of Indonesian Film Producers (Aprofi). The long-term aim is to seed French-Indonesian co-productions. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘SNL’: Druski Dons Whiteface as Elizabeth Holmes in ‘You Can See Everything’ Parody Billy Evans Addresses Amanda Seyfried’s Portrayal of Elizabeth Holmes in 'You Can See Everything’: She Was ‘Eager’ to ‘Play a Character’

"Indonesian filmmakers have never lacked stories. What they have lacked is structured access to international partners," said Fauzan Zidni, chairman of BPI. "BPI is committed to working with the Ministry of Culture, the French Embassy, CNC and our industry associations to make sure these projects get made."

French script consultant Eric Collins leads the story development strand, working with each team individually to sharpen each project's artistic vision and international prospects. A separate two-day industry workshop covers development, financing, international distribution and the workings of the French film business. It is led by producers Vincent Wang of House On Fire and Thibaut Amri of Avant La Nuit, along with Sébastien Chesneau of sales company Cercamon.

The selection comprises "A Straight Way to Love," written and directed by Kurnia Alexander and produced by Eliza Cheisa; "An Interesting Incident," directed by Rizal Hanun, who co-wrote it with producer Janice Angelica; "Father Figure," from writer-director Rizaldy Bagas and producer Mo Amputra; "My Tears, a Sea for Jakarta to Sink," written and directed by Andrea Nirmala Widjajanto and produced by Nirartha Bas Diwangkara; "Saltstorm!," from writer-director Al Ridwan and producer Utari Hanif Assyuri; and "Super Neli," co-directed by Robby Ul Pratama, who also produces, and Anggi Frisca from a script by Resty Savira Oktaviani and Sally Anom Sari. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"It is particularly fascinating to discover how strongly traditional culture resonates in contemporary Indonesian storytelling," said Julie Tingaud, deputy head of international affairs at La Fémis.

Teams from last year's edition get their next shot in December. The inaugural Southeast Asia Film Forum takes place in Paris Dec. 9-13, hosted by France's CNC, the Centre Pompidou and the French cultural network. Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines are the four partner nations, and the program mixes panels, screenings and an institutional strand around a central slate of co-production meetings.

Indonesia's presence will be backed by the Ministry of Culture's film directorate. BPI will take part in the institutional program, filmmaker Edwin will present two of his films, and the 2025 lab teams will pitch to French producers.

Fabien Penone, France's ambassador to Indonesia, Timor-Leste and ASEAN, said the lab built on the joint cultural strategy adopted by French President Emmanuel Macron and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto at Borobudur on May 29, 2025, and that last year's duos would arrive in Paris after a year of mentoring from La Fémis. "This is precisely our ambition: to turn the growing ties between our two film industries into concrete and long-term collaborations and, ultimately, more co-productions between France and Indonesia," Penone said.

The Borobudur declaration calls for a closer, more formal audiovisual alliance between the two countries, with co-production as its centerpiece. The Yogyakarta lab is one of the ways the two countries are building it.

The JAFF Market runs alongside the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival .

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The MCU's Avengers and FOX's X-Men are finally coming together in Avengers: Doomsday , and only a few heroes have the ability to unite them. The Doomsday trailers hint that the Avengers and the X-Men will fight at the X-Mansion, meaning that their initial meeting will probably see the teams take opposite sides.

However, other shots in the trailer imply that the Avengers and the X-Men will team up, most likely to take down Doctor Doom. If the universes of both sets of characters are at risk, it will probably be difficult to get the teams working together. However, these three MCU characters just may be able to do it.

Despite only having one appearance in the MCU so far, in 2022's Black Panther: Wakanda Forever , Namor the Sub-Mariner has already become one of the franchise's most complex characters. Namor's immense commitment to Talokan puts him in opposition to the Wakandans in his debut film, although he isn't necessarily a villain. Instead, Namor is an isolationist and a nationalist, something that makes it easier for him to make the hard choices.

Wakanda Forever confirmed that Namor is a mutant, giving him a direct connection to the X-Men characters who will appear in Doomsday . We aren't entirely sure why Namor is in the film, but having him bridge the gap between the heroes of his home universe and his fellow mutants would be the perfect reason. Namor is a major player in Avengers: Time Runs Out , the comic series that Doomsday seems to be taking heavy inspiration from. So, his involvement in the incursion between the various universes could cause him to seek a diplomatic way to ensure his home's survival.

After the end of Loki season 2, the titular Asgardian is the new He Who Remains, sitting at the End of Time and overseeing the multiverse. The Doomsday trailers have already confirmed that Loki has a role in the film, and one of the Avengers: Endgame Encore bonus scenes shows Loki paying Steve and Peggy a visit after the end of the film. As the MCU character who is arguably most knowledgeable about the multiverse, it makes sense for him to intervene in the incursion between the two universes, especially because Loki isn't scared to meddle in the fates of other worlds.

So, if Loki can find a way to save both universes, he will probably step in. Since so many of Doomsday 's main characters are still clueless about the multiverse, Loki may need to explain what's really going on to the Avengers and the X-Men. He may be able to point them toward Doom as the true threat, uniting them against the film's main villain. After all, Loki should have knowledge of what Doom is up to well before any of Doomsday 's other characters, and his visit to Steve Rogers could signal that he is uniting a team of multiversal heroes to take Doom down.

Unlike the other two heroes on this list, Monica Rambeau hasn't yet been confirmed to appear in Avengers: Doomsday . However, she is the hero in the best position to unite the Avengers and the X-Men. After gaining her powers in WandaVision , Rambeau appeared as a proper superhero in 2023's The Marvels . Since The Marvels is one of the MCU's least-successful films, many fans of the franchise don't know that it contains one of the best Doomsday setups.

At the end of The Marvels , Monica finds herself trapped on the other side of a multiversal rift, with Carol Danvers, Kamala Khan, and Nick Fury unsure of what happened to her. Then, the film's post-credits scene reveals that Monica has awoken in another universe, where she is being watched over by a variant of her mother as well as Kelsey Grammer's Beast. Since Grammer also played Beast in 2006's X-Men: The Last Stand , this was a confirmation that some of FOX's X-Men would return in the MCU. However, this post-credits scene has never been touched on since.

Grammer's Beast is one of the X-Men characters who will return in Doomsday , and while Monica Rambeau isn't confirmed to appear, this is too good of a setup to ignore. The Avengers could come across Monica while in the X-Men universe, with her bridging the gap between the two sets of heroes. Her time with the X-Men could give her information that is key to the incursion events that will appear in Doomsday , clearing up the conflict between the heroes and preparing them for the battle ahead.

Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars , Emmys , Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change in response to buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.

Golden Globes Predictions Commentary (Updated: Nov. 24, 2026): Golden Globe voting is underway! Here's the breakdown of all the submissions.

Eighty-eight films were submitted for best motion picture (drama), and 43 are competing for best motion picture (musical or comedy). Among the drama submissions are Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” and Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three.” The musical or comedy field also includes Destin Daniel Cretton’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”

In the lead acting races, the drama category for best actor has 69 submissions representing 64 performers with Brad Pitt in contention for “Heart of the Beast,” alongside Robert Pattinson for “Primetime.” The musical or comedy category features 32 submissions from 31 performers, including Tom Holland for “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and Ryan Gosling for “Project Hail Mary.”

The best actress (drama) race has 39 submissions from 39 performers, with Zendaya (“Dune: Part Three”) and Anne Hathaway (“Verity”) among the contenders. The musical or comedy field has 23 submissions from 22 performers. Meryl Streep returns as Miranda Priestly in “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” while Olivia Wilde earns two entries, for “I Want Your Sex” and “The Invite.”

The acting races are led by the supporting actor category, which boasts 221 submissions from 198 performers, making it the most crowded of the six acting fields. Mark Ruffalo has three entries in the supporting category alone: “Being Heumann,” “Crime 101,” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” The supporting actress category has 158 submissions from 146 performers. Florence Pugh appears twice, for “Dune: Part Three” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” while Zendaya is also a double entrant, with submissions for “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day" that go along with her two leading bids.

Behind the camera, 131 filmmakers are attached to 123 films in the best director race, including Steven Spielberg for “Disclosure Day” and Nolan for “The Odyssey.” The screenplay category features 121 submissions, among them Quentin Tarantino’s script for “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” and Drew Goddard’s adaptation of “Project Hail Mary.”

The music categories include 100 submissions for best original score, with John Williams (“Disclosure Day”) and Hans Zimmer (“Dune: Part Three”) among the composers in contention. Best original song has 51 entries, including Taylor Swift and Jack Antonoff’s “I Knew It, I Knew You” from “Toy Story 5,” as well as two submissions from Diane Warren.

The animated feature category has 24 eligible films, including Andrew Stanton’s “Toy Story 5” and Brad Bird’s “Ray Gunn.” Meanwhile, 42 films are submitted for best motion picture (non-English language), including Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s “All of a Sudden,” representing Japan, and Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love,” representing South Korea.

The cinematic and box office achievement category features 20 submissions, among them “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” starring Streep, and surprisingly, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth." Across all categories, 170 distinct films have been submitted, while the six acting categories account for 475 different performers.

articles.title: 5 Characters Who Are Perfect Love Interests for Batman Who Aren’t Catwoman
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Depending on the day, Batman is either the most popular or second most popular superhero in the world, only competing for that role with Spider-Man. Of course, a character as storied and in-demand as the Dark Knight is bound to have his fair share of relationships. Romance sells, after all, and Batman has never been […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Depending on the day, Batman is either the most popular or second most popular superhero in the world, only competing for that role with Spider-Man. Of course, a character as storied and in-demand as the Dark Knight is bound to have his fair share of relationships. Romance sells, after all, and Batman has never been the best at maintaining a normal relationship, which has given rise to a whole armada of potential lady loves . The most popular is definitely Catwoman, and I'd argue that she's the best every day of the week, but she's far from the only incredible woman who would make a great partner for Batman. Today, we're looking at five non-Catwoman ladies who each bring something incredible to Batman's stories.

If Catwoman is Batman's number one love, then Talia is his second great love, although she definitely makes a strong case for that top spot. She's definitely left her impact on Batman's mythos, between being the daughter of the infamous Ra's al Ghul, often helping Batman stand against her villainous father, and bringing Damian Wayne into the world as Bruce's first and, at this time, only biological child in canon. Traditionally, Talia has always had a torrid relationship with Bruce, where both long to be with the other, but their dedication to pursuing saving the world their own way constantly drags them apart.

Their connection has definitely soured over the years, especially when she took a much harder turn into stereotypical villainy, but as they've picked up the pieces, they definitely bring a new version of this old dynamic back to life. There's clear tension between them, especially in how they raise Damian, but seeing them co-parent the young Robin is always a treat. Their interactions feel more like a divorced couple who still love each other, and exploring how that affects raising their son has already given us plenty of fun stories.

Scarlett is a newer entry on this list, first appearing in Detective Comics #1090, but her history is intimately tied to Bruce's, as she is the daughter of Joe Chill. As it turns out, Martha and Thomas Wayne helped Scarlett's mother escape her abusive relationship with Chill, with said mother going on to become the deadly Asema to honor the Waynes. However, Scarlett never wanted to hurt anyone. In fact, she's dedicated her life and scientific genius towards helping people however she can , which is what brought her into contact with Bruce in the first place.

The idea of Bruce dating Joe Chill's daughter is a strange but strangely resonant one. Batman has always been a story of growing from pain, and Scarlett is just as haunted by her parents as Bruce is, just in reverse. They both want to turn their grief and despair into fuel to make the world a better place, and Scarlett having an active role in helping Batman would be a narrative redemption of sorts for Chill, bringing a part of Batman's origin full circle. At the very least, this deserves exploration.

Catwoman and Talia aren't Bruce's only supervillainess lovers, and while Nocturna might be the most forgettable of this troupe, she still has the potential to bring something really interesting to the table. She started out as a woman with photosensitive skin who could teleport and emit irresistible pheromones, but post- Flashpoint appearances have taken the full leap towards making her a vampire. She and Batman had a blossoming romance that would be cut short by her apparent death in Batman #391, and she wouldn't make a major appearance as a love interest again. For him, anyways, as Nocturna did seduce and manipulate Batwoman for a time.

What really makes Nocturna an interesting candidate for this is that she's legitimately terrible for Batman. She's a greedy, selfish villain who can mind control people using their own desires, but its those imperfections and connection to the dark that would bring something unique to the table. Despite how often his relationships tend to blow up, most of them end due to misunderstandings or bad timing, not because the characters truly aren't compatible. Nocturna brings all of the bad-girl energy from Batman's greatest loves without any of the heart that makes them work, which is new ground for a Bat-relationship. Also, the jokes about Batman dating a vampire practically write themselves.

Silver is a very unique love interest. She began as a typical Gotham City socialite who had sparks fly with Bruce, but after she noticed his continuous disappearances, she puzzled out his secret identity all on her own. Unfortunately, the stress of losing Bruce to his second life as Batman was too much, and she left him. Still, the flame never truly died for either of them, and they would continue to love each other even years later. Silver brings something special to Batman's life in the sense that she reminds him how to have fun. She definitely has her own struggles, but she makes Bruce smile in a way that is incredibly rare to see.

If nothing else, Silver would ensure that we get more stories focusing on Bruce's place in society. We rarely get stories where Bruce actually has to live as anything more than Batman, but Silver is the perfect character to bring those types of stories to the forefront. She could also help flesh out the Gotham City upper-crust, which, despite appearing so often, remains rather underdeveloped aside from some crime bosses. Silver could breathe new life into a part of Gotham we've never seen before and put a smile on Batman's face.

Annika Zeller is actually Batman's current love interest, with the as-of-yet unreleased Batman (2025) #18 boasting a cover where the two kiss. The chemistry between them is abundant, and the sparks are flying, with the two even going on a date in issue #5. Zeller is a brilliant doctor at Arkham Towers, developing a device known as the Crown of Storms, which would help even the most insane of criminals balance their minds and take a legitimate step towards recovery. She prioritizes people first and foremost, which is what Batman sees in her in the first place, but she also brings plenty of drama to the table.

Zeller is open about her disapproval of Batman , and while she's willing to work with him, she fundamentally disagrees with his methods. This provides natural tension that the pair will have to work through, and gives Bruce a great person to bounce off of and rein him back when he pushes too far. She's a balancing factor to Batman's most out-there tendencies, and he is the person who helps her see beyond the Arkham walls. Most importantly, Zeller still hopes that people can change, which is something Batman always needs reminded of, as his ultimate mission is to help everyone. They disagree on methods, but their missions couldn't be more similar.

Which Bat-love interest do you think brings the most to the table? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Twilight Fans Have Been Talking About That James Bond Scene. There’s Even More To It Than We Thought
articles.summary: Before he was 007, he was Cullen. Edward Cullen.
articles.content:
When it was announced that Robert Pattinson had been cast as James Bond , Twilight fans everywhere did a little cheer. Especially if you were Team Edward ! What a good long-term investment that’s turned out to be! However, the most popular Twilight -related reaction to Pattinson being 007 stems from the fact that the iconic spy was brought up in the vampire movie. As it turns out, there’s a whole new layer to that scene we didn’t know about.

Isn’t that wild? James Bond is literally said in Twilight right before the current James Bond appears. However, there’s more to it. The movie’s director, Catherine Hardwicke, revealed something new about the scene while talking about the casting on The Kyle Buchanan Show . In her words:

That happened 18 years before it became a reality. I guess it goes to show the role has been right for Robert Pattinson all along given those on the set of Twilight were thinking about it, too. Pattinson didn’t earn the role easily, either. All sorts of other eligible actors such as Nicholas Hoult, Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden reportedly auditioned for Denis Villeneuve’s film. Charlie Cox also recently said he was shot down for being “too old” even though he’s just three years older than Pattinson.

While it’s perhaps a bit surprising Amazon MGM Studios didn’t opt for an actor who was an unknown , Jeff Bezos has said that in the screen tests it was “so obvious” Pattinson was their Bond that they didn’t dare pick anyone else. We can’t wait to see what his Bond will be like, and given his career thus far, it sounds like it might be unexpected.

The Academy’s Visual Effects Branch notified the artisans behind the 20 films advancing to the next round ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Through multiple sources, Variety has confirmed 19 of the finalists, including Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three,” Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s “Project Hail Mary,” Steven Spielberg’s “Disclosure Day” and Marvel Studios’ “ Avengers: Doomsday ” from Anthony and Joe Russo. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'One & Only’ Campaign: BOTOX® Cosmetic (onabotulinumtoxinA) Has Been FDA Approved for Over 20 Years Andrew Scott on Starring in ‘Elsinore’ and Feeling ‘Very Grateful’ to Be an Out Gay Actor

Disney leads the confirmed titles with four. Alongside “Avengers: Doomsday,” the studio lands Jon Favreau’s “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu,” 20th Century Studios’ “Whalefall” and Thomas Kail’s live-action “Moana,” which brings Dwayne Johnson back as the demigod Maui.

Skydance (formerly Warner Bros Discovery) took three of the spots: “Dune: Part Three,” Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s Tom Cruise-led “Digger” and Craig Gillespie’s “Supergirl” from former DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran. But the studio also sees four contenders fall short.

Villeneuve’s stakes are historic. Both “Dune” and “Dune: Part Two” won the visual effects Oscar, and in March, “Avatar: Fire and Ash” made James Cameron’s franchise three-for-three in the category. “Dune: Part Three,” which opens Dec. 18, now puts Villeneuve two steps from the same trilogy sweep. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Universal Pictures booked both of its summer event films, “The Odyssey” and “Disclosure Day,” while Amazon MGM Studios goes two-for-two with “Project Hail Mary” and Kyle Balda’s “The Sheep Detectives.”

Nolan’s track record in the category is just as formidable. “Inception,” “Interstellar” and “Tenet” each won the visual effects Oscar. However, the branch famously left “Oppenheimer” off its top 20 for the 96th Academy Awards. Spielberg has been here before, too, with “Jurassic Park,” which won the category in 1994.

Two of the more intriguing finalists come from outside the Hollywood studio system. Takashi Yamazaki’s “ Godzilla Minus Zero ” follows “Godzilla Minus One,” which won the category at the 96th Oscars and delivered the franchise its first Academy Award. Laika’s stop-motion “Wildwood,” directed by Travis Knight, gives the studio a chance to return to a category it cracked with Knight’s “Kubo and the Two Strings,” one of only two animated films ever nominated for visual effects, along with “The Nightmare Before Christmas.”

Sony lands three big movies in the field. Leading the charge is Destin Daniel Cretton’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and the still-to-be-released “Jumanji: Open World” advancing alongside “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” the Indian mythological epic. “Ramayana” follows S.S. Rajamoulili’s “RRR,” which reached the top 20 for the 95th Oscars and signals the branch’s continued appetite for large-scale spectacle from outside Hollywood.

A24 also lands a spot with “Backrooms,” the feature directorial debut of 21-year-old Kane Parsons, whose YouTube series turned the internet’s liminal-space legend into a box office phenomenon, grossing more than $400 million worldwide.

Paramount received a split verdict. David Ayer’s survival thriller “Heart of the Beast,” starring Brad Pitt, advanced, but Variety confirmed that two of the studio’s other contenders, “Ebenezer” with Johnny Depp and the video game adaptation “Street Fighter,” did not make the top 20.

Netflix also breaks through with Peter Berg’s epic war drama “The Mosquito Bowl,” one year after the streamer placed “Frankenstein” and “The Electric State” on the shortlist. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That leaves one spot unconfirmed, with a few titles still awaiting confirmation. Variety will update this story as additional finalists are confirmed.

articles.title: 'Dancing With the Stars' Finalist Connor Wood Has Already Won: "I Feel Really Good"
articles.summary: The 31-year-old comedian has made it to the finale of the dance competition series show, even though he never quite expected it: "I really can't put my finger on why this clicked for me, but I leaned in a lot."
articles.content:
Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood has become a bit of a fan favorite on this season of Dancing With the Stars . "If we're not in practice, I feel like I'm missing practice," the 31-year-old tells The Hollywood Reporter on a Zoom call. It's a rare rainy day in Los Angeles, and the season 35 contestant is finding a second to rest amidst crazy rehearsal schedules.

He and partner Rylee Arnold have taken each challenge in stride. The pair have found themselves amongst the five couples advancing to the show's finale , airing Tuesday night. Wood's viral social media moments have certainly helped endear viewers, however, his steadily improving dancing skills don't hurt. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'Dancing With the Stars' Season 35 Couples Perform Their Last Dances as a Winner Is Crowned in the Finale: See the Scores, Who Won (Updating Live) TV Where to Stream 'Dancing With the Stars' Season 35 Finale Live Online

"I have been really intentional about my life and making sure I don't ever work really hard," he says, cheekily. "This has changed that completely, flipped it on its head."

Heading into the final episode, he and the dancers are working with six hours a day of rehearsal to get themselves in prime condition. "Every minute of that is necessary for the show," he notes.

Below, Wood speaks with THR about heading into the DWTS finale, the reaction to his viral Jennifer Lawrence moment and dealing with the online hate.

How do you feel going into the finals?

I feel really good. Me and Rylee, we went into the semifinals, and that was the hard part. It was two brand new dances, two long dances, two very fast hard dances, and this one is fun. We're going out there, we're putting on a show. It really is for us, which is fun. It's for the fans, [but] it's [also] for us. It's something that hasn't been seen before. We're doing a really cool dichotomy of dances too. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

What days are the longest for you?

The day after the show, we film basically what you see before we dance. We do all of the face-to-face interviews. We do the one-on-one interview, and then we do the group session interview. This is obviously a bigger one. There's three dances, so they have three videos that they had to make. There's one for each dance, and then they'll film rehearsal and stuff for the filler. But I also have the podcast that I do, so that was 9 a.m. to 12 p.m., and then we filmed from 12 p.m to 10 p.m.

It was long, but it's all needed. That's the thing. Sometimes you go onto a set or something, and it's like we're doing a take for the 15th time, and I'm like, "I promise you I'm getting worse. Every time we do another one, I promise you're getting a worse take from me." This is not the case. This one you do get better as you put more hours in, which is an annoying, frustrating thing that that is true. The harder you work, the better you get.

articles.title: After The Last Jedi Backlash, Would Rian Johnson Return To Star Wars? Someone Asked Him
articles.summary: I personally loved The Last Jedi.
articles.content:
Generations of moviegoers were brought up on the Star Wars movies , and the franchise continues to expand thanks to live-action shows available with a Disney+ subscription . The sequel trilogy ended a few years ago, but there's still discourse surrounding Rian Johnson 's subversive sequel The Last Jedi . The movie got some backlash, but would the filmmaker still return to the galaxy far, far away? Someone recently asked him.

Talk about a glowing review. Clearly the time away from the franchise hasn't quelled Rian Johnson's fond feelings for The Last Jedi . And while we never got his announced Star Wars trilogy , he stands by both the process and the final product that hit theaters back in 2017.

I'll take it. While not an all-out confirmation, Rian Johnson hasn't ruled out the possibility of returning for another Star Wars movie. The franchise has been away from the big screen for a few years, but that'll change in 2027 with Shawn Levy 's Starfighter . Fingers crossed that the Knives Out filmmaker eventually gives it another spin in the beloved science-fiction property.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With the Avengers: Doomsday release date drawing ever closer, the reveals just keep coming, and now, that has included a brand-new Doomsday teaser that shows previously unseen footage of two original Avengers facing off against Doctor Doom. Already, this week has brought a shocking number of Doomsday updates, most notably the final Doomsday trailer , which prominently featured Steve Rogers, confirming, among other things, that Steve and Bucky will finally reunite and that he has a somewhat grown son (who looks to be about preteen age).

On the heels of that trailer and the fanfare that followed it, a new Entertainment Weekly article comprised a number of updates and reveals, to an explanation for why certain X-Men are missing from Doomsday to new insight about Doctor Doom from Robert Downey Jr. , specifically regarding the differences between Tony Stark/Iron Man and Doom. As if that wasn't exciting enough, this new teaser for Doomsday is showing some all new looks at the film, including a showdown that fans will no doubt be eager to see. Check out the teaser and more about this upcoming face-off below.

It doesn't really come as any surprise that Steve Rogers and Thor will be facing off against Doctor Doom in Doomsday . After all, we've already seen that Thor and Doom go head to head in prior trailers for the movie, and with Steve clearly being such a central figure, especially following that most recent trailer, it was only a matter of time. Even so, it's cool to get a first look at that actual meeting (assuming that this is the first meeting) in the teaser, which shows Thor and Steve together approaching Doom and his throne.

New international teaser for ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ In theaters on December 18. pic.twitter.com/poFeuTql8Q

However, this teaser also comes as a reminder that the Avengers really do have an uphill battle in this movie. In addition to Doctor Doom's power, which is already known to be immense and world-ending, Doom currently has both the Hulk and the Scarlet Witch on his side, following the post-credits scenes in Spider-Man: Brand New Day and VisionQuest , respectively. We also don't yet know who the other Latverian witches are, assuming that Wanda Maximoff is one of them, which feels like a safe bet at this point, and it's possible that Doom has collected other characters, like Spider-Man and even Doctor Strange.

With all of that in mind, and considering Thor's unfortunate line in the Doomsday trailer about him not even knowing half of the heroes present, this feels like an even more impossible task than the fight against Thanos in Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame . And, considering that Avengers: Secret Wars is already confirmed to be releasing next year, it seems like the Avengers will probably lose before they win, not unlike those aforementioned movies.

Do you think the Avengers have a chance against Doom? Let us know (and why) in the comments below.

articles.content:
In a surprising reveal, Arnold Schwarzenegger ’s son, Joseph Baena, has announced that he’ll be in the upcoming Baywatch reboot. Primarily known for his previous appearance as a contestant in Season 31 of Dancing with the Stars , his background in bodybuilding and his physique make it a no-brainer that he’s found his way onto the beach.

Upon joining Baywatch ’s cast , model Livvy Dunne put on one of the iconic red swimsuits and got to work alongside the OGs, also making appearances . It sounds like Joseph Baena was quite impressed with the work the cast has put in.

The 29-year-old half-sibling of Patrick Schwarzenegger admitted he didn’t watch the original Baywatch series when it premiered on TV. Instead, he became a fan of David Hasselhoff when he was in the SpongeBob movie, where there was a playful homage to the show and his character.

Since we’ve only seen glimpses and teases of footage, it’s hard to get a sense of the show’s tone, the new character dynamics, and just how epic the action will be on a weekly basis. However, with the new generation of lifeguards being led by Hobie ( Stephen Amell ), the son of the iconic Mitch Buchannon (David Hasselhoff), and a number of the OG cast members returning, the hype and the nostalgia are real and should easily get an audience tuning in.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Christopher Nolan has become renowned as one of the best directors working in Hollywood, and along with his work on movies like Oppenheimer , the Dark Knight Trilogy, and his epic take on The Odyssey , Nolan has made some of the most narratively mind-bending movies of the last three decades. All the way back in 2000, long before he would receive his first Oscar or be granted $250 million budgets, the director make his first major impact on the industry with a movie with a fractured story that really made audiences pay attention to what was happening on screen. That movie was Memento , starring Guy Pearce as a man with memory loss , who attempts to piece together a sequence of events to uncover the mystery of how he ended up in the position he is in when viewers first join his story. For those who have not seen the movie, or simply want to revisit it, if you are a Netflix subscriber your time to do so is running out as the movie leaves the platform on December 1.

Memento centers on Leonard Shelby, who suffers from anterograde amnesia after an attack that led to the death of his wife. His memories of the life he had before the attack are intact, but new memories only stay with him for a short time before he forgets them. On a quest for vengeance against his wife's killer, Leonard builds a map of Polaroids, notes and body tattoos to help him piece together the events that he can no longer remember and finally get his revenge. While this could sound like a regular film with a simple storyline of a wronged man on a road to ruin, Nolan's genius move is to tell the story across two timelines in a piece of fractured storytelling that puts viewers into the life of Leonard and his distorted memories.

Many years after making Memento , Christopher Nolan would completely baffle audiences with his reality-twisting Inception , but the same kind of highly detailed direction and plotting was all there way back in his first big hit. Memento breaks the story of Leonard into two distinctive timelines; one in black and white showing Leonard taking a phone call in motel room and one in color, told in stages in reverse chronological order that slowly piece together the mystery of the film in the same way Leonard recalls them. The movie concludes with the two timelines converging in a final revelation and bringing to a conclusion one of the most riveting and accomplished movies of Nolan's career despite his subsequent huge successes.

The movie was made for just $9 million and easily became a hit with a $48 million box office return. As well as being hailed as a masterpiece in storytelling by both critics and audiences (with Rotten Tomatoes scores of 93% and 94% respectively), the film also received Academy Awards nods for Best Original Screenplay and Best Editing, the latter of these really being what made the movie what it is. It also established a blueprint that Nolan would utilize frequently in his movies, with fractured storytelling, manipulation of time, and emotional-driven lead protagonists playing a part in many movies such as Tenet , Dunkirk, and, of course, Inception . However, it is hard to imagine any of those movies without Memento . For anyone who has not seen the film, it is certainly worth seeking out on Netflix before the end of the month, and while it may not get you in the Christmas mood, you will get a movie a that is hard to forget.

Is Memento still one of Christopher Nolan's best movies? Let us know what you think in the comments.
