articles.content:
Philip Rosenberg, a production designer and art director who was part of the team that won the art direction-set decoration Oscar for " All That Jazz ," died Oct. 28 in West Palm Beach, Florida. He was 91.

His death was announced by his nephew, Alan Rosenberg.

Rosenberg's first film job was as design assistant on the 1968 "The Sea Gull." He went on to become an art director and production designer, working with New York-based directors such as Sidney Lumet, Paul Mazursky and Norman Jewison. He partnered with production designer Tony Walton on films including "The Wiz" and "All That Jazz." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Chris Colfer Says 'Glee' Reboot 'Conversations' About Kurt's Return Are Ongoing: 'From What I Heard, It Sounded Very Funny and Like a Good Idea' Jane Lynch Wants to Return for 'Glee' Reboot: 'I Would Love to Do Sue Sylvester for the Rest of My Life'

Known for being part of the realist school of production design in the 1970s, he was nominated for an Oscar as art director of "The Wiz." Among his other credits were "The Owl and the Pussycat," "Next Stop Greenwich Village," "The Gambler," "Network," "The Sentinel," "Running on Empty," "Night Falls on Manhattan" and "Moonstruck." His final credit came for "Collateral Damage" in 2002.

Rosenberg grew up in Prospect Park South, Flatbush, Brooklyn, and studied scenic design at Yale. After graduation, he was hired as an assistant at the Metropolitan Opera, as well as assisting Marcel Vertès on the murals in the Cafe Carlyle.

He married Siv Sandstrom, a hostess in the Swedish pavilion at the 1964 World's Fair, who assisted him in the art department on films including "Running on Empty" and "Moonstruck." She died in 2024.

He is survived by his brothers Stanley Rosenberg and David Rosenberg and six nieces and nephews.

articles.title: One of the 80s' Most Inappropriate Superheroes Somehow Got His Own Children's Toy Line
articles.summary: The Toxic Avenger is tasteless, crass, and about the last thing you'd expect to see propping up a toy line for children. But somehow, Playmates decided to turn Toxie into an action figure line with 1991's Toxic Crusaders, tying in to the just-as-inexplicable Toxic Crusaders cartoon that aired a brief thirteen episode season that same […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Toxic Avenger is tasteless, crass, and about the last thing you'd expect to see propping up a toy line for children. But somehow, Playmates decided to turn Toxie into an action figure line with 1991's Toxic Crusaders , tying in to the just-as-inexplicable Toxic Crusaders cartoon that aired a brief thirteen episode season that same year. Who thought this was a good idea? A clue lies within the manufacturer of the Toxic Crusaders toyline: Playmates. In 1988, Playmates had a surprise monster hit with their Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles action figure line, which was still the most popular action figure line on the market in 1991. With its similar premise of "mutant hero born out of toxic waste," it wasn't that far-fetched to imagine kids having a similar response to The Toxic Avenger . And while the source-material from Troma wasn't exactly kid-friendly, neither were the original Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles comics from Mirage. The series and its toys may not have lasted long, but like everything else ever to emerge from Tromaville, they have built a dedicated cult following.

No definitive reason has ever been settled on for what happened to the Toxic Crusaders series and figures. Alternately, controversy over the R-rated source material and general marketplace oversaturation have been blamed: the early nineties were a golden age for both intellectual-property based cartoon series and tie-in toylines. The expansion of cable television meant that there were now far more networks with competing children's programming, inspiring series we're still talking about today . Most of them, however, met the same fate as Toxic Crusaders , lasting for only a season and condemning their tie-in toylines to languish on-shelves. The Playmates Toxic Crusaders line was not a strong seller, but the enduring cult popularity of the Toxic Avenger toyline has given it a second-life with action figure collectors, who are willing to pay a premium for rare, end-of-line release like the Apocalypse Attackcopter vehicle .

Nine figures and five vehicles were produced for the Toxic Crusaders line. With their neon-colors and gross-out sculpts, the resemblance to Playmates' Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles line is unmistakeable. The good guy faction was headed up by the Toxic Avenger himself, joined by Major Disaster, Nozone, Headbanger, and Junkyard. The line's four villains were led by Doctor Killemoff, joined by henchmen Psycho, Bonehead, and the Radiation Ranger. Each figure came packaged with a special glow-in-the-dark accessory, which came sealed in a plastic bag, labeled "SECRET TOXIC GLOW-IN-THE-DARK WEAPON: SO RADIOACTIVE WE'VE PUT IT UNDER WRAPS." Three to five additional weapons and accessories were included with each figure, finding them complete poses a significant challenge to collectors today. Especially sought-after is the Toxic Avenger's signature mop, without which the figure just doesn't look right.

Nozone is the most "gross-out" character in the line, featuring an exaggeratedly-giant nose (hence the name), as well as sculpted splatters of snot all over the figure. He's a former test pilot, mutated by flying through a hole in the ozone layer. After a crash-landing into a radioactive silo filled with pepper, the toxic chemicals in Nozone's body grant him the mutant ability to produce powerful sneezes. Tongue was firmly in-cheek when these characters were created, to be certain. Headbanger's origin calls DC's Firestorm to mind, while his design evokes Masters of the Universe 's Two-Bad : a scientist and a singing telegram fall into an atom-smasher, merging into a single being. Headbanger is at first one of Doctor Killemoff's henchmen, but switches sides after discovering the Toxic Crusaders get more dates (really). Junkyard is also the result of a fusion, a half-man, half-dog created by lightning-striking a toxic waste contaminated homeless man and his pet. Major Disaster is comparatively bland: he's a soldier who gains the ability to control plants from a radioactive swamp, a little like Man-Thing or Swamp Thing .

Doctor Killemoff is a native of the planet Smogula, trying to terraform (Smogulaform?) Earth into a polluted world akin to his ravished home-planet. He wears a breathing apparatus, depicted as an elaborate, multi-piece accessory, to help him survive in Earth's toxic fresh air. Psycho is his bio-mechanoid lackey, and possesses powers of prognostication that go ignored by his master: every episode, Psycho is able to accurately predict how the Toxic Crusaders will foil their plans. Bonehead is an acid-rain scarred punk and former enemy of the pre-transformation Toxic Avenger, now anointed commander of the "Radiation Rangers," Killemoff's force of mutant foot soldiers. Additional villain characters like the monstrous "Polluto" were featured in the series, though the toyline was cancelled before they could be given a plastic counterpart.

Somehow, Toxic Crusaders occupied the confluence of three trends. Most immediately, there was an early nineties trend of environmentally-conscious children's cartoons, with these themes cropping up in Captain Planet and the Planeteers and Swamp Thing as well as Toxic Crusaders . Besides Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, it was the prevalence of these series that convinced Troma and their partners to move ahead with Toxic Crusaders . The other trends were longer-term, and less easily explained. Beginning in the mid-eighties with series like Rambo: The Force of Freedom and RoboCop , animation studios and TV networks looked to R-rated film properties to provide recognizable franchise names for their children's series. The principle made sense: R-rated franchises and characters had the allure of "forbidden fruit" to children, and these series would let them see them in action. Other times, companies like Kenner would go ahead with a kid-ified version of a property like Aliens or Predator without a tie-in series, trading on the existing adult name of the franchise alone. There was a somehow-unforeseen drawback: parents.

The parents of these children were also familiar with properties like Aliens, RoboCop , and The Toxic Avenger, and it's been suggested they played a key role in the demise of these toylines and cartoons. Although largely apocryphal, the contention is that parents just weren't comfortable with these grown-up franchises being marketed to their kids, and wouldn't buy the toys or let them watch the tie-in. The most significant backlash was seen in the late eighties, when parent groups successfully had several companies' Nightmare on Elm Street children's toys discontinued. However, these factors also contribute to the aftermarket for these toys, drawing adult collectors them decades later. Some are just fans of the property, fascinated by the sheer weirdness of Toxic Avenger action figures. Others are those same kids whose parents wouldn't let them collect the line back in 1991, finally making good on the desires of their eight-year-old self. Either way, Toxic Crusaders has become one of the stranger footnotes of its era, forgotten by most toy collectors, but passionately collected by a dedicated cult following.

articles.title: Demon Slayer Peaked Early, But Infinity Castle Can Save It
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Ufotable The Demon Slayer anime peaked early thanks to its first season and movie, but the series still has the potential to surpass that success. The reason for its early success wasn't its epic storytelling but rather Ufotable's fascinating anime adaptation. The studio captivated anime fans worldwide with its vibrant animation, showcasing modern animation at its […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Demon Slayer anime peaked early thanks to its first season and movie, but the series still has the potential to surpass that success. The reason for its early success wasn't its epic storytelling but rather Ufotable's fascinating anime adaptation. The studio captivated anime fans worldwide with its vibrant animation, showcasing modern animation at its peak. However, what followed after the first season was the anime movie adaptation of the next canon arc from the manga, which is where the series truly peaked. It showcased a level of animation that surpassed everything else up until then.

First released in Japanese theaters in late 2020, the anime movie became a huge success. With the manga also approaching its conclusion at the time, the movie boosted manga sales exponentially, helping the series reach 150 million copies in total sales. Since then, the series has gained another 70 million copies in sales, surpassing 220 million as of this writing . However, despite two more seasons and another movie, the series has yet to match the heights it reached early on. The Infinity Castle trilogy, however, can surpass that achievement by building on what the franchise has already accomplished, and it is already doing so.

Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle was a huge success for the franchise and at the box office, earning more than $200 million compared to Mugen Train . On paper, this already suggests that it is a bigger success than its predecessor. However, the main element Infinity Castle had going for it was its animation, which, despite being an improvement, was something fans had already come to expect. Many fans even believed that the movie should have been an anime season instead, as it essentially felt like nine episodes consolidated into a single film. That said, while its emotional impact may have fallen short compared to Rengoku's death, the first movie has laid the foundation for what is to come next.

This is exactly what makes the next two movies' potential to surpass it and reach even greater heights so exciting. The second movie will likely include two major events, potentially featuring the battles against Upper Moon Ranks One and Two. Once again, this could make the second movie feel like an entire season compiled into a single film. If that happens, the final installment, featuring the all-out battle against Muzan, could be the one that truly feels like a movie. As the final installment in the Demon Slayer franchise, it has the potential to elevate the series to even greater heights, surpassing what it has already achieved.

In other ways, the Demon Slayer franchise has already excelled, from its animation to its compelling and emotional storytelling. To surpass that foundation, bringing the climax to the big screen is what could truly solidify the franchise's legacy as a visual masterpiece. The Demon Slayer franchise is already on a different level , having reached heights that fans might not have expected it to surpass. However, if the franchise aims to go even further and save itself as an anime that will be remembered for more than just its animation, it will need to stick the landing with its final film, something the concluding installment of the anime has the potential to achieve.

articles.title: HBO's Harry Potter Reboot Confirms Big Change From the Movie Costumes That's Book Accurate
articles.summary: HBO HBO's Harry Potter TV series will be the Christmas present that the entire world gets this year, and hopefully it's one they want to keep. The series will offer a long-form version of what a generation of fans got from the Harry Potter films, and (hopefully) will take readers of the books on a much […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google HBO's Harry Potter TV series will be the Christmas present that the entire world gets this year, and hopefully it's one they want to keep. The series will offer a long-form version of what a generation of fans got from the Harry Potter films, and (hopefully) will take readers of the books on a much more complete and familiar journey. As the premiere date gets closer, we're seeing much more of what the finished production looks like, and diehard fans are spotting some pretty fine details that show the level of fidelity the show is showing to the text.

The latest set of Harry Potter promotional images showcases a milestone moment from the first novel, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone : Harry Potter's first trip to Diagon Alley, the hidden magical market where all Wizards and Witches go to shop for their mystic essentials. However, fans are also taking note of something else in the image: the fashion Harry is wearing before he gets some proper wizard's robes.

The official Harry Potter website posted a new featured article titled "Six fashionable findings from the HBO Original Harry Potter series costume department". It helps viewers get a deeper sense of the intense level of detail that was put into the show. The first item on the list is "How to spot magical people in the Muggle world," and it features the above image of Harry Potter (actor Dominic McLaughlin) taking in the wonder of Diagon Alley, while wearing an outfit that very much looks like what a '90s kid would be wearing.

In the breakdown, the style and design team behind Harry Potter describe how they had to create a sense of fashion for the Wizarding World that felt like it could plausibly exist alongside the fashion of non-magic humans (or "Muggles") of the time. That meant "a lot of synthetics. The costume department scoured charity shops and rag-and-bone yards, consulting their family albums for unglamourous ensembles to represent early 90s fashion: unfiltered."

There's also an interesting amount of logic that went into guiding the style choices for the series: "Magical people don’t stick to trends," the site states. "They would likely ditch high street shops for jumble sales, culminating in more eclectic, unconventional wardrobes. Don’t expect all witches and wizards to look the same."

There's an even deeper dive into the fashion of Harry Potter (2026), check it out on the franchise's official site .

The Harry Potter movies that Warner Bros. put out started in 2001 with Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone , and ended in 2011 with Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2 . The studio chose to update the story to a modern-day setting (at that time), meaning that characters wore 2000s fashion trends to make them relatable to audience members of similar age. It raised some ire with hardcore fans of the books, as there are some deeper metaphors and symbolism about real-world politics and culture at that time, which were invariably altered by the time shift.

Now, the TV series is going the opposite route with its period piece format. It'll be interesting to see how viewers react to that, and if the book-accurate setting really does change or enhance the experience of the story, in visual form.

Harry Potter will premiere on HBO on Christmas Day. Do you like the '90s look?

articles.title: Charles Barkley Pitched His Potential Inside The NBA Replacement, But I Have Another Idea
articles.summary: This isn't a bad pick, but another host is on my mind.
articles.content:
As Inside the NBA ’s latest season on ESPN continues, questions continue to swirl around the show in regard to its future. Longtime co-host Ernie Johnson has officially confirmed his plans to leave the show at the end of this season, and colleague Charles Barkley apparently plans to do the same. There’s been a lot of discussion regarding who might replace the beloved sports commentators, and Barkley recently pitched his successor. While it’s a solid pick, I’d admittedly prefer to see another seasoned pundit take over Barkley’s post.

Barkley – also known as “The Round Mound of Rebound” to some – is definitely someone who loves to speak his mind. So it doesn’t surprise me at all that he’d have thoughts on who might be able to take his place on Inside . The former Phoenix Sun was recently quoted as saying he didn’t believe anyone but fellow ex-player Jalen Rose could replace him at the desk. That comment was brought up to Rose when he was interviewed by Front Office Sports (as seen on YouTube ) and, when asked about the job, he said this:

The notion of Rose taking over for Barkley is actually quite reasonable, considering his resume as a broadcaster. He’s not only served as a fill-in analyst for Inside the NBA for years now, but he’s also taken on hosting duties for ABC/ESPN over the years. I personally enjoy seeing Rose when he appears on Inside , and his relaxed demeanor usually serves as a firm counterbalance to others on the dais like the vivacious Barkley or Shaquille O’Neal . With that said, there’s another recurring analyst I’d love to see join the show instead.

Inside has welcomed plenty of insightful and entertaining guest hosts over the years, from the cool Vince Carter to the wise-cracking Draymond Green (who has a rivalry with Charles Barkley) . Someone who, for me, has always been a welcome presence on the show is Chris Webber, who’s been appearing on the show for years. He obviously has plenty of broadcasting experience, and he’s a wealth of knowledge when it comes to basketball. I’d say the show would be lucky to have him full-time.

Again, though, this isn’t to say that Jalen Rose wouldn’t be able to do the job effectively. There may actually be a reality in which both players end up on the show full time by next season. However, that’s assuming ESPN is looking to bring on two former players and not get another non-ex-player analyst to specifically fill the void that’ll be left by Johnson.

To be honest, it may also behoove me not to get too ahead of myself right now, as the season is still young. Also, while Charles Barkley’s retirement claim is seeming more likely , he hasn’t said much more about it in the wake of Ernie Johnson’s announcement. We’ll just have to wait and see what happens and how the producers choose to proceed should Barkley leave the fold along with Johnson.

articles.title: Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving Special Isn't Good, But There Are 5 Reasons To Still Watch it
articles.summary: A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving from 1973 is arguably among the least thrilling of the Peanuts' animated antics, especially from the retro era of the cartoon. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving from 1973 is arguably among the least thrilling of the Peanuts' animated antics, especially from the retro era of the cartoon. Even Charlie Brown himself seems tired of his holiday specials, remorsefully lamenting to Linus, "We've got another holiday to worry about." While I agree with his sister Sally's complaints about how she has barely finished her Halloween candy, this cartoon offers very few memorable gags and seems more contrived than it does original. What it lacks in standing out among its dozens of peers , it makes up for it in a few ways that shockingly make it worth the watch.

Charlie Brown is off to visit his Grandmother to celebrate with his family, but his plans are interrupted by Peppermint Patty when she invites herself over to his home to spend the holiday. He finds himself in an even worse predicament when his guest list grows from one classmate to many more, and he's forced to figure out how to entertain and feed an entire cavalcade of kids. As if the general feeling of existential dread and anxiety that Charlie Brown walks around with on a daily basis wasn't enough, now he has to figure out how to roast a turkey when all he knows how to do is burn toast and pour milk on cereal. It sounds straightforward, and it is — but the road to that festive meal includes a handful of elements that make this Thanksgiving cartoon something to add in your holiday viewing rotation.

Peppermint Patty is an iconic part of the Peanuts cast, but she wasn't an original one when the strip debuted back in 1950 (although there was someone named Patty but these two characters are not the same). It wasn't until Aug. 1966 that the green-shirted brunette first stepped her sandals onto newspaper strips. This was the same year that It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown! first hit the airwaves on CBS, but there would be six more animated specials in between this Thanksgiving toon before we finally saw her in an animated format.

A friend of "Chuck's" as she prefers to call him, Peppermint Patty inserted herself into Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving plans rather abruptly, but in her mind she was entitled to his attention. Throughout her time in the series, Patty has shown an interest in the yellow-shirted blockhead that goes beyond friendship. She's very forward with him on the phone, leaving him blushing and at a loss for words. While it isn't shown in this special, Patty's companion Marcie also has a crush on the same guy — something he has zero ability to handle. Charlie Brown is not much for romance and is the furthest thing from a casanova, so it's funny to watch him in these situations where he probably enjoys the attention from a girl but has no idea what to do with it.

Vince Guaraldi had been working with Charles Schulz and the Peanuts gang as far back as 1963, predating the first animated Christmas special. Alongside his trio and later quintet, Guaraldi composed and played his jazz stylings through a dozen Charlie Brown cartoons, with this one among the group. If the Christmas soundtrack was more melancholy and the Halloween special a bit more serious and spooky, the Thanksgiving special is more upbeat and light-hearted to match the nature of its story.

Guaraldi's updated reprise of "Linus and Lucy" for Snoopy's cooking montage is a jam that keeps on giving, adding more flair to one of his most well-known jazz compositions that has become the theme song for the franchise. Where the soundtrack shines the most is "Little Birdie," a song that introduces Woodstock into the mix during this toon. The majority of Guaraldi's work on the series were instrumental, but "Little Birdie" is one of the few songs across the series that has lyrics, but one of a very tiny selection that the artist sang by himself. His expressive and soulful voice backed by sounds of brass and bass is extremely catchy and will stick with you long after the memory of the cartoon disappears.

There are some pretty solid visual gags throughout the Thanksgiving show, including one of my favorite sequences with Snoopy brawling against a lawn chair in a clash of champions that is not as one-sided as you might think. But throughout the entire show, it's Woodstock who steals the show as the funniest element that keeps the audience laughing and wondering what he will do next. It's impossible not to love the tiny yellow bird, and he adds a ton of comedy relief alongside Snoopy. Their relationship is often more Laurel & Hardy, with Snoopy using his size to make some jokes about their power dynamic, but Woodstock always shines and makes sure both buddies come out on top.

Besides helping Snoopy cook the non-traditional Thanksgiving meal (more on that in a second), Woodstock joined his pal in dressing up as pilgrims in a very silly segment that involves a luggage trunk and some oversized hats. If Snoopy and Woodstock came from overseas to colonize my people, I'd be a little less apprehensive about it than a ship full of British people. Woodstock simply makes everything better, and he was another great addition to the Peanuts roster that brought a ton of energy to this otherwise bland affair.

Since Charlie Brown is catering a meal for kids who aren't allowed to use a stove without parental guidance, he does the rational thing and employs his dog and bird friend to do all the cooking. Snoopy puts on his adorable chefs hat and gets to work, making popcorn and buttered toast to accompany their side dishes of jellybeans and pretzel sticks. If you were a child making dinner who had no idea how to cook, this is basically what you would do. Anyone can operate a toaster, even a canine who may or may not have opposable thumbs.

Snoopy would make Martha Stewart proud, decorating a ping-pong table with a lovely linen cloth and origami-folded napkins. While it's all very nice, what upsets me is Snoopy's lack of beverages for the kids. Mysterious pink sundae cups appear on the table during the feast with no explanation (and we're never shown who made them or what they actually are), so we can assume whatever cherry-topped concoction in there is in place of their drinks. If I was eating all that salt, dry bread and tooth-decaying snacks, I'd want something to sip on, but we can only expect so much. After all, Snoopy needed time to work on his pilgrim costume with Woodstock. He has his priorities, but we appreciate him making the time and putting in the effort to feed this makeshift group.

Peppermint Patty might think Charlie Brown is cute, but her patience for his spontaneous Thanksgiving party is practically non-existent. Besides inviting herself over without asking, Patty rudely complains to the entire party about the meal and berates him in front of the guests. It isn't until Marcie reminds her compatriot that she was never actually asked to come, and may have hurt his feelings with her brusque words. Charlie Brown takes it to heart and worries he ruined Thanksgiving for everyone, but Marcie reminds him that they should all be thankful to be together while Patty apologizes for playing "lover's games" and the group reconcile.

In the end, all of the kids are invited to Charlie Brown's grandmother's condo to celebrate Thanksgiving. Meanwhile, Snoopy and Woodstock stay home and enjoy a secret traditional meal with the yellow bird eating one of his distant cousins with a smile. That might be the most memorable thing about this special, but I'm choosing to ignore that one because I don't want to have Charlie Brown levels of anxiety thinking about Woodstock as a cannibal. But what should stay with you more is how the ultimate message in this cartoon was a very practical lesson in gratitude. The main course is "Be happy with what you have and not what you don't" with a side of "friends are family," differentiating it from other Thanksgiving specials that focus on just the general idea of being thankful. It's a bit more nuanced and surprisingly mature for a kids cartoon, but we shouldn't expect less from a boy named Charlie Brown.

Do you have any memories of the Charlie Brown Thanksgiving special, or maybe a different nostalgic cartoon about Turkey Day? Join the conversation and let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: Marathon Reveals New Bishop Shell With One of the Game's Coolest Trailers Yet
articles.summary: Bungie has created one of its best cinematic trailers yet for Marathon's newest Shell, Bishop, which is saying a lot considering how great the studio is at these. Each Shell trailer showcases the character, but this is easily one of the most impressive and stylish. In it, Bungie reveals Bishop, a striking new Shell that […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Bungie has created one of its best cinematic trailers yet for Marathon's newest Shell, Bishop, which is saying a lot considering how great the studio is at these. Each Shell trailer showcases the character, but this is easily one of the most impressive and stylish. In it, Bungie reveals Bishop, a striking new Shell that immediately gives samurai robot vibes. There is no doubt this Shell will be a popular pick once it drops as part of Marathon's Symbiote update and future plans. The trailer teases some possible aspects of the Shell's kit, but we won't know its full capabilities just yet.

Bishop was previously teased as part of Marathon 's upcoming Symbiosis update , which is scheduled to launch on December 8. However, Bungie's latest cinematic offers a much better understanding of the playstyle the developer wants to encourage with the new Runner Shell. While most players would probably want to maintain some distance between themselves and their enemies in an extraction shooter, Bishop appears to thrive in close-quarters combat. Between its intimidating appearance, incredible speed, and devastating melee capabilities, the new Shell looks like something ripped straight out of a samurai fan's dreams, and that's certainly not a bad thing for Bungie's shooter.

Bungie shared the new Bishop Shell cinematic on November 24, accompanied by the tagline, "BISHOP SHELL // HUNTER KILLER. STRIKE ONCE, STRIKE FAST." Sporting a striking red chassis, an extendable blade, and leg-mounted thrusters, Bishop systematically hunts down an opposing crew throughout the trailer. The robot uses firearms alongside throwing knives, showing the diversity of its kit.

However, it's the closing moments of the cinematic that really steal the show. After being shot by an opportunistic Rook, Bishop lowers itself into a combat stance, extends its blade, and uses its thrusters to rapidly dash toward its opponent, delivering a devastating melee strike reminiscent of classic samurai films. If this is anything to go by, Bishop could be exactly the shakeup Bungie needs to keep Marathon interesting and afloat .

Mobility is king in Marathon and Bishop appears to have that in spades. It could be great at crossing open areas, and extremely deadly when fighting inside buildings or navigating narrow corridors. An aggressive Bishop player could potentially close the distance before an opponent has time to reposition, making encounters particularly unpredictable.

Of course, the cinematic isn't representative of actual gameplay, and Bungie has yet to fully detail Bishop's abilities, cooldowns, or damage output. Balancing such a mobile, melee-focused character will undoubtedly be important. Bishop is also just one reason to be excited about Marathon 's Symbiosis update. Bungie is introducing Expedition, a permanent PvE mode featuring roguelite elements, alongside an experimental 3v3 Team Deathmatch mode. Marathon's future is looking up , and Bishop is just one part of that.

As summer draws to a close, the theatrical release of Children of Blood and Bone draws nearer.

The film adaptation of Tomi Adeyemi’s YA fantasy is directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood , and it stars quite a stacked cast of actors and characters.

For everything we know about the Children of Blood and Bone movie, read on.

When will Gina Prince-Bythewood’s Children of Blood and Bone come out?

The film will arrive in theaters January 15, 2027 as one of the first highly anticipated releases of the new year.

Thuso Mbedu , who worked with both director Prince-Bythewood and costar Viola Davis on The Woman King (2022), will star as the main character Zelie. Amandla Stenberg ( The Hate U Give , The Acolyte ) will portray Amari. Damson Idris ( F1 , Snowfall ) will play Inan. Tosin Cole ( Supacell ) will portray Tzain.

Davis will portray Mama Agba. Cynthia Erivo ( Wicked ) will portray Admiral Kaea. Idris Elba ( Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw ) will play Lekan. Lashana Lynch ( Bob Marley: One Love ) plays Jumoke, and Chiwetel Ejiofor ( 12 Years a Slave ) plays King Saran. Regina King ( Shirley ) will appear as Queen Nehanda. Diaana Babnicova will portray Folake and Buuky Bakray will portray Binta.

Saniyya Sidney ( Fences ),  Zackary Momoh  ( Harriet ), Richard Mofe-Damijo ( Namaste Wahala ), Ayra Starr, Pamilerin Ayodeji ( Mikolo ), Shamz Garuba ( Crime and Justice Lagos ), Kola Bodunde ( Shadow ) and Temi Fagbenle rounded out the cast later on. Ayodeji and Garuba were cast through an open casting call in Nigeria.

Is there a trailer for the Children of Blood and Bone movie?

Yes, a trailer was released in late July, introducing the cast and their characters as Orïsha faces a battle for its magic. What is Children of Blood and Bone about?

The first novel in the Legacy of Orïsha trilogy chronicles Zelie's journey to restore the intrinsic magic to the land after King Saran made a move to purge it, seeing it as a threat and unnatural. Drawning on African mythology, the fantasy setting contains groups of humans that practice magic known as Maji. The Maji divine certain elements, and thus are known by the specific powers they wield, from water workers beckoning tides to those like Zelie's mother Jumoke, who can summon souls.

Zelie and her brother team up with the son and daughter of King Saran. Prince Inan (Idris) has doubts about taking on his father's crown and following King Saran's example directly.

What artists will have music in the upcoming Children of Blood and Bone movie?

Tems serves as the soundtrack executive producer, and has contributed "African Love Song" which is featured in the film's second trailer. Beyoncé's "Energy (feat. Beam)" featured in the first trailer. Guest features on the soundtrack include:

Is Tomi Adeyemi involved in the movie adaptation of Children of Blood and Bone ?

Adeyemi co-wrote the screenplay with Prince-Bythewood. She has expressed that she won’t watch the film, and she posted a video on Instagram explaining her experience on set.

Are there more Children of Blood and Bone books? Will there be more movies?

Yes, the book gave way to a trilogy. Following Children of Blood and Bone 's publish date in 2018, Children of Virtue and Vengeance arrived in 2019, and Children of Anguish and Anarchy arrived in 2024.

There are currently no plans to adapt the next two books in the series into films.

Does Tomi Adeyemi have other books?

Adeyemi has The Siren coming out at the end of September.
